title: Dynamic equilibrium
examples: Teacher, what does 'dynamic' mean in this context?
Can you explain what a closed system is using an example?
How does temperature affect the equilibrium point?

explain.say: Today we are learning about dynamic equilibrium in chemistry.
First, we must understand what a closed system means.
A closed system means nothing passes across its boundaries.

draw.text: No exchange of matter or energy

explain.say: Next, let us look at reversible reactions in chemistry.
This means the reaction can go both forwards and backwards.
Dynamic equilibrium means the forward and reverse rates are equal.

faq.q: What does 'dynamic' mean when we talk about equilibrium?
faq.a: It means that the reaction is constantly happening in both directions. The rates are equal, but the substances are still changing.
asks: Does it mean nothing is changing?

faq.q: If a system is in equilibrium, does that mean the reaction has stopped?
faq.a: No, the reaction has not stopped at all. It is happening continuously, but the rates of the forward and reverse reactions match.

faq.q: Why must the system be closed to observe equilibrium?
faq.a: If matter can escape, the concentrations change, and the balance we are trying to measure will be lost.
asks: Why can't we use an open system?

faq.q: What is the difference between a reversible and an irreversible reaction?
faq.a: An irreversible reaction goes only one way, while a reversible reaction can go both ways, eventually reaching equilibrium.
asks: Is one way or two ways?

faq.q: Can I change the temperature to shift the equilibrium?
faq.a: Yes, changing temperature or pressure can shift the balance towards one side or the other.
asks: How do I change the balance?

facts: Dynamic equilibrium occurs when the rate of the forward reaction equals the rate of the reverse reaction.
A closed system prevents the exchange of matter with the surroundings.
Reversible reactions are represented by the double arrow, shown as '<=>'.
At equilibrium, the concentrations of reactants and products remain constant.

quiz.say: A sealed container containing reactants and products is an example of a:
quiz.why: A closed system prevents matter from leaving or entering the container, allowing equilibrium to be observed.

wrong.0: While related, 'closed' specifically means matter cannot escape, which is the key concept here.
wrong.1: This describes the reaction, not the physical boundary of the container.
wrong.3: An open system allows matter to enter or leave, changing the balance.

quiz.say: The double arrow '<=>' indicates that the reaction is:
quiz.why: The double arrow shows that the reaction can proceed in both the forward and reverse directions.

wrong.0: Dynamic describes the state of the rates, not the arrow itself.
wrong.1: Static implies no change at all, which is incorrect for an equilibrium.
wrong.3: This means the reaction only goes in one direction, never returning.

quiz.say: At dynamic equilibrium, what is the relationship between the forward and reverse rates?
quiz.why: Equilibrium is defined by the rates balancing each other out, even though the substances are changing.

wrong.0: If the rates were always changing, the system would not be at a stable equilibrium.
wrong.2: If the forward rate were zero, the reaction would have stopped completely.
wrong.3: If the reverse rate were zero, the reaction could only proceed forward.
